paragraphs.text: The veil and the youth first. Naught of folk stands toward Your veiling. Naught of lovers either. Though won by method-ladder-steps, though thick with epithets: to love-sharers, Thou, the self, at once, pure, dawns. Winning even, laugh too; won even, laugh too: muddy, drinking Thy love-nectar, whoever indeed, Lord. May I never dry up, never seek release: brimmed with Thy-love-sap, best-tasted, past-topped. As unmet before, this Thy-love-sap of mine befell: so, Ruler, may that same fatten. Truly, Lord: no other prayer’s reach is mine. Only be that, somehow some, love’s seizure mine, ever.

Then the frenzy catalogue, letting everything in. Love-drunk even: may I rage, for Becoming rue, laugh, up leap, yell Shiva. Enough. Pit-standing even, hale even, weeping even, laughing even: deep even, scatter-minded even, may I be, by love, Ruler. For lovers naught to be felt: in Thee within, or without — where Thou, knowing-natured, doubtfree standest, Thyself. Lovers, at blame-mimicked even, thrill: by Thy nectar-drops, as if, inward-pierced by keen thrill-needles. Pain-feeling even, for lovers, ripens to feasting: whose knowing, all of it, nectar-wet, is Thy-moonshine-made. Where-go held, of lovers, without-within: guileless, Thy-frame-touch-sap-taste-joy same. Lord, in Thy love’s worship, the abject share that leans on two wiped out, some savor a frame clear, nectar-made. Astray, ford-seers, split: for split is but straying’s. Foeless, thing one: for lovers Thou shinest. Mind stainless-ripe past honor, scorn, love and the rest: whose is he, the lover? World-like-mannered how could he be? Love-hate-gloom even, whose love-shine conquered: before those great ones, which are the knowing-rich? Whose rite-and-means is love-nectar-bath-and-drink: his, in begun-middle-end states, high ease-seat. Praised be, sought be, worshiped be: whereby Thou alone, of Thy lovers, praised be world-faring, Thee-made.

Then freedom, then seal. Freedom’s name is but ripe love in Thee, Lord. Thereon, first-stage-mounted, freed-like are we. Pain’s coming even, great be mine, love-brimmed-souled. From-Thee-turned, All, never: joy’s train even. Thou by love art gladdened; love, gladdened in Thee: and, Lord, since that mutual-ground is fit, as Thou alone knowest it. Shaped or shapeless, in or out even: to lover-selves, Ruler, ever art Thou nectar-made. In this world itself, within, toward Thy lover: joy-showing-fruited, another world-stand stands. In the hidden, love; in the high, love; in the world’s Great Lord, love: in Thee, Kind One, in Shiva — love, forsooth, some! Ah! Love, love: high love, fierce love indeed! Loud I wail: let fierce love be mine, high love, in Thee. Since I am all beauties’ birth-ground, Ruler: in Thee stuck, priceless be jewel or straw. From knower to known, on whose feeling-road by Thee no parting is: they win, Thy partakers. Outside passing’s hall, by some art Thou clasped: Master. But by others, right there, drooping, rein-dropped. With BhavAnI — drinking, eating, decking, feasting the all-world whole — dissolution-feast-hurried, hard-clasped Shiva I bow.
